cards.alt: Sample multiple choice card: Which is most often cited as an exception to strict cell theory?

questions.stem: A new antibiotic selectively blocks the 30S ribosomal subunit. Why is it relatively safe for human cells?
options: Human ribosomes lie in the nucleus
Human cytosolic ribosomes are 80S with 40S small subunits
The antibiotic cannot cross the plasma membrane
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes have 70S ribosomes (50S + 30S). Eukaryotic cytosolic ribosomes are 80S (60S + 40S) and are not blocked. Human cells do have ribosomes, they are in the cytoplasm and on the ER, and drug entry is not the selectivity mechanism.

questions.stem: A membrane permeable only to water separates 0.2 M glucose on the left from 0.1 M NaCl on the right. What happens?
questions.explanation: NaCl gives two particles, so 0.1 M NaCl is 0.2 Osm, equal to 0.2 M glucose (0.2 Osm). With equal osmolarity there is no net water flow, so neither direction is favored. Solutes cannot cross, so NaCl does not move either.

questions.stem: A mutation prevents the LDL receptor from binding clathrin adaptors. LDL will
options: bind the cell surface but not be internalized
questions.explanation: The receptor still recognizes LDL, but clathrin-coated pit formation needs the adaptor interaction, so uptake fails. Binding is intact, so it does bind, internalization is not normal, and extracellular degradation is not a feature.

questions.stem: Severe diarrhea occurs from a mutation that makes intestinal tight junctions leaky. The most likely explanation is
options: paracellular passage of solutes and water
questions.explanation: Tight junctions limit paracellular movement. When leaky, solutes and water pass between cells. Gap junctions do not seal the epithelium, hemidesmosomes anchor to the matrix, and endocytosis is unrelated.

questions.stem: Which finding best supports the bacterial origin of mitochondria?
options: Mitochondria are found in nearly all eukaryotes
Mitochondria have a circular genome and divide by fission
Mitochondria contain proteins encoded in the nucleus
questions.explanation: A circular genome and binary-fission-like division resemble bacteria. ATP production and widespread distribution do not show origin. Nuclear-encoded mitochondrial proteins reflect gene transfer, not an origin as such.

demo_cards.front: State the three tenets of classical cell theory.
demo_cards.back: All living things are made of one or more cells; the cell is the basic unit of structure and function; all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

demo_cards.text: Prokaryotic ribosomes are {{c1::70S}} (50S + 30S); eukaryotic cytosolic ribosomes are {{c2::80S}} (60S + 40S).
demo_cards.extra: S is the Svedberg sedimentation unit, so subunit values do not add up to the whole.

demo_cards.stem: Which molecule crosses a lipid bilayer fastest by simple diffusion?
demo_cards.why: Small nonpolar gases pass freely. Glucose is large and polar and ions are charged, so both need proteins.

demo_cards.statement: Viruses count as living cells because they carry out their own metabolism.
demo_cards.why: Viruses are acellular and have no metabolism of their own. They replicate only by hijacking a host cell, which is why they are the classic challenge to cell theory.
